answer.rationale: The 18% cost mandate and 14-day renewal window create urgency, but the 94% assembly line utilization means delivery risk is the binding constraint. Verification of memory_c4 (successful renegotiation recovered margin and moved incumbent on price/terms) and memory_c2 (low-cost vendor switch worked operationally) will inform whether aggressive negotiation with the incumbent can achieve the cost target while preserving supply stability. The incumbent has demonstrated responsiveness to benchmarking pressure (c4) and multi-year commitments unlock volume pricing (c6). A targeted negotiation campaign leveraging market benchmarks and our cost requirement offers the highest probability of meeting the 18% target without the migration risk of switching (which c2 shows works operationally but requires onboarding time we don't have) or the complexity of adding a second source mid-cycle. This preserves the option to switch or dual-source if negotiation fails, while using the current renewal trigger to extract concessions. If negotiation yields <15% savings, we defer and execute a vendor switch in the next cycle with proper staging.
